items.headline: Meta Raises €9 Billion as Euro Bond Debut Draws Record Demand
items.excerpt: Meta Platforms Inc. raised €9 billion from a debut euro debt bond sale that drew a record €53 billion of orders — the most for any corporate deal in Europe — after offering generous yields that even investors cautious about the AI boom found difficult to pass up.

items.headline: CVS Plans to Break Up $117 Billion Healthcare Conglomerate
items.excerpt: CVS Health plans to spin off its retail pharmacy business into a new company called CVS Pharmacy in the first half of 2028. The move will separate the drugstore business from the Aetna insurance unit and Caremark prescription benefits division, with both companies to be publicly traded. Bloomberg's

items.headline: Kiwi Slide Haunts New Zealand’s Main Parties Ahead of Tight Vote
items.excerpt: New Zealand’s weakening currency is compounding the cost-of-living pressures turning voters away from the country’s main political parties ahead of next week’s election.

items.headline: Musk’s Texas Gamble Becomes Liability With Democrats Taking Over
items.excerpt: Elon Musk at least was able to put a comical twist on the Republicans’ midterm meltdown, infused with his signature doses of dark humor and needling of adversaries.

items.headline: Wall Street Sees Risks to AI Boom After the Democratic Sweep
items.excerpt: While stocks rallied as the Democratic sweep of Congress promises to exert a significant restraint on President Donald Trump, one key corner of the market was left out.

items.headline: HP Appoints Emma Walmsley as CEO, Concluding Executive Search
items.excerpt: HP Inc. named former GSK Plc chief executive officer Emma Walmsley as its new CEO, permanently filling the role after HP’s Enrique Lores departed earlier this year.

items.headline: Qualcomm to Build Equipment for SpaceX’s US Mobile Network
items.excerpt: Qualcomm Inc. will supply hardware components for SpaceX’s planned nationwide terrestrial wireless network, the latest sign that Elon Musk’s rocket and satellite company is committed to challenging the biggest players in the US mobile industry.

items.headline: Crypto Giants Scrap Crime-Fighting Alliance as Hackers Circle
items.excerpt: An initiative set up by some of crypto’s largest companies to curb illicit activity has quietly been dissolved, at a time when crime involving digital assets continues to surge.

items.headline: CoreWeave Bonds Hit New Lows as Texas Data Centers in Crosshairs
items.excerpt: CoreWeave Inc.’s bonds tumbled on Wednesday, in some cases to new lows, after Democratic candidates in favor of slowing down data-center construction won a number of gubernatorial races, including in Texas.

items.headline: Cyberattacks on Cryptocurrency Targets, Supermarket Fridges Serve Geopolitical Purpose
items.excerpt: Americans’ trust in societal institutions is near record lows.

items.headline: Wayfair Growth Reaches Post-Pandemic High on US Share Gains
items.excerpt: Wayfair Inc.’s revenue grew at the fastest pace since the pandemic-driven e-commerce boom, as the home furnishings retailer continued to boost its overall order numbers against a challenging consumer backdrop.

items.headline: Africa-Focused OPay Is Said to Halt US IPO After China Inquiry
items.excerpt: Inquiries by a Chinese regulator prompted Nigeria-focused payments company OPay Ltd. to halt its $300 million US initial public offering just hours after setting the price, according to people familiar with the matter.

items.headline: Online Supermarket Unicorn Rohlik Weighs Prague IPO, CEO Says
items.excerpt: Rohlik Group is weighing an initial public offering in Prague as one option for taking the Czech online supermarket public.

items.headline: Waymo Co-CEO Says Uber App Deal Was ‘Crapshoot’ for Riders
items.excerpt: Alphabet Inc.’s Waymo Co-Chief Executive Officer Tekedra Mawakana said her company’s plan to end an exclusive robotaxi partnership with Uber Technologies Inc. was in response to customer feedback asking for more consistency when ordering self-driving services.

items.headline: Waymo’s Bet on a Driverless Future
items.excerpt: Emily Chang travels to San Francisco to meet Tekedra Mawakana, Waymo’s co-CEO. Chang asks Mawakana how a career overseeing technological pivots prepared her for the top job and how she navigates safety concerns, growing competition and building public trust in a technology with much to prove.

items.headline: Vauban Seeks More Investments in European District Heating, Fiber, Data Centers
items.excerpt: Vauban Infrastructure Partners is seeking opportunities to invest in European district heating and fiber networks, as well as data centers and battery storage — assets it sees as resilient to any economic downturns.

items.excerpt: The Bloomberg Tech event looked ahead to new balance of power in US

items.headline: Cyberattackers Drain Money From French Bank Credit Mutuel Arkea
items.excerpt: Crédit Mutuel Arkéa said hackers stole money from it after gaining access to its computer systems, underscoring the growing cybersecurity risks for the banking sector.

items.headline: How Markets Reacted to Democrats’ Win: Stocks U-Turn, Gold Gains
items.excerpt: Global stock markets erased a selloff sparked by a Democratic sweep of the US Congress, as uncertainty surrounding the midterms faded and dip-buyers rushed back into a bruised market.
